subject: Tidal Retail: intermittent 5xx + checkout latency spikes
messages:
From: Marta Ruiz <marta@tidalretail.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwoodai.com>
Cc: NetworkOps <netops@tidalretail.com>
Date: Fri, 09 Oct 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Tidal Retail: intermittent 5xx + checkout latency spikes

Hi Irene,

We're seeing a recurring spike in checkout latency and a ~20% increase in 5xx errors hitting Redwood's inference endpoints that we use for product descriptions. The first spike started ~08:00 PDT and we've had repeated ~30-90s bursts since then. Attached is a screenshot of request latency and a short time window of our app logs.

Impact: checkout page renders slowly for ~8–12% of users; some sessions report 'failed to load suggestions' and fall back to static copy. This is causing increased cart abandonment (we saw a 4% uptick).

Can you confirm whether this looks like a Redwood-side network problem (peering, NAT, or DNS) vs something on our edge? We're scheduled for a leadership review at 11:30; would appreciate an update before then.

Thanks — Marta
Marta Ruiz
Head of Platform, Tidal Retail

Attachment: screenshot_latency_graph.png (image)
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwoodai.com>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta@tidalretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodai.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwoodai.com>
Date: Fri, 09 Oct 2026 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Tidal Retail: intermittent 5xx + checkout latency spikes

Hi Marta — thanks for the heads up. We're treating this as P1. I'm looping in the on-call infra and the customer-facing SE.

Quick asks to help us triage:
- Can you share a 1–2 minute tcpdump or packet capture from one of the affected worker nodes (client->Redwood edge) if possible?
- Are you seeing any DNS errors (NXDOMAIN/timeout) in your app logs?
- Approximate POPs/regions from where you see the spikes (we can correlate with our edge telemetry).

We're spinning up traceroutes and checking VPC peering metrics + NAT gateway scaling logs now. Will update within 30 minutes.

Irene
Irene Choi
Sr. Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

Note: forwarding your screenshot to infra for reference.
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodai.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwoodai.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwoodai.com>
Cc: Marta Ruiz <marta@tidalretail.com>
Date: Fri, 09 Oct 2026 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Tidal Retail: intermittent 5xx + checkout latency spikes

Quick interim notes from SE side:
- Customer traffic pattern shows very bursty token usage every ~15s from their checkout workers.
- On our side, there are elevated SYN retransmissions from a subset of client IPs aligned with the customer's POPs.
- I asked the customer for a tcpdump; they provided the screenshot only so far.

Hypothesis: could be transient path instability on the peering / intermediate transit (BGP flap or transient route bounce) leading to packet reordering and connection resets that surface as 502/504 at their app level. Another possibility is that our edge proxy is intermittently classifying the flows and sending them to a throttled backend group.

I've scheduled a 09:30 bridge with Tidal + Infra to correlate packet captures and edge logs. Jonas — can you pull NAT gateway metrics and recent firewall proxy rule changes for their account?

— Marissa

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwoodai.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwoodai.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodai.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwoodai.com>
Cc: NetworkOps <netops@tidalretail.com>, Lee Chen <lee.chen@cloudexchange.net>, aws-nw-eng@amazon.com
Date: Fri, 09 Oct 2026 09:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Tidal Retail: intermittent 5xx + checkout latency spikes

Summary of infra triage (09:10–09:40 window):
- Collected traceroutes from our POPs to Tidal's announced prefixes. We observed intermittent AS path changes and one brief BGP withdrawal (09:18 PDT) for the primary peering path.
- Edge proxy logs indicate a small cluster of connections where the backend pool returned 502; those requests line up with periods of increased retransmits and socket timeouts.
- NAT gateway CPU/connection metrics show a transient spike in concurrent ephemeral port usage coincident with the customer's large bursts — this caused short-lived port exhaustion on a subset of NAT instances in us-west-2.

Attachments: tcpdump_20261009.pcap (pcap, 28MB) — contains a sequence showing retransmits and a TCP RST after a missing ACK. Also attached edge_route_snapshot.txt with BGP peer state during the incident.

Immediate mitigations applied:
1) We rerouted affected customer traffic to a secondary transit path while we stabilize the peering (automated route failover applied at 09:36).
2) Scaled NAT pool capacity for the customer's dedicated egress group (manual provisioning in progress).
3) Disabled a recent experimental proxy backpressure rule that was causing a small percentage of connections to be queued under high burst.

Next steps: collect the customer's packet capture, coordinate with Cloud Exchange partner (Lee) to validate upstream peering behavior, and keep the customer updated.

— Jonas
From: aws-nw-eng@amazon.com <aws-nw-eng@amazon.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwoodai.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwoodai.com>, NetworkOps <netops@tidalretail.com>
Date: Fri, 09 Oct 2026 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Tidal Retail: intermittent 5xx + checkout latency spikes

Hi team,

We investigated the AWS side for the us-west-2 path. We observed a short-lived control-plane event at 09:17 PDT that caused a partial route withdrawal to one of the transit nexthops; BGP reconverged within ~18s but that coincides with the customer's retransmit window. We don't see persistent packet loss after reconverge.

Recommendation: keep the temporary route diversion in place for 24 hours while we monitor. We'll also open a support case and share detailed control-plane logs. Case ref: https://support.aws.amazon.com/case/123456789

Cheers,
AWS Network Eng
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwoodai.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwoodai.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwoodai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodai.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwoodai.com>, Marta Ruiz <marta@tidalretail.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 17:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Incident summary: Tidal Retail checkout latency & 5xx (10/9) — exec brief

Team — brief summary for exec awareness and next steps.

Impact: 4–8% increase in checkout latency for Tidal Retail users during ~08:00–10:00 PDT on 2026-10-09; repeated short bursts of 5xx errors, customer-reported cart abandonment impact; business sensitivity high.

Root cause (contributing):
- Short-lived control-plane routing event on upstream transit (BGP withdrawal) that overlapped with customer request bursts, causing packet retransmits.
- Local NAT ephemeral port exhaustion on a subset of NAT instances for Tidal's dedicated egress group — amplified impact of the transient path issue.
- An experimental proxy backpressure rule caused some connections to be queued and time out during the event.

Actions taken: route failover to secondary path, scaled NAT capacity, rolled back proxy rule, engaged AWS support and Cloud Exchange partner. We collected packet captures and edge logs (attachments).

Customer ask: Tidal has requested a formal incident RCA and goodwill credits for the period of degraded performance. They also want confirmation of steps to prevent recurrence.

Proposed follow-ups:
1) Complete full RCA write-up (network timeline + mitigation) by 10/14.
2) Automated NAT scaling for high-burst customers by Q4; immediate rule: increase ephemeral port headroom for dedicated egress groups.
3) Harden routing failover and add a synthetic probe from customer POPs into our edges for early detection.
4) Commercial: propose a one-week service credit and a joint postmortem call with the customer week of 10/19.

Please advise if you'd like a short briefing for the board or if we should route this through account execs only.

Thanks — Irene
